newsitem.title: USA: MAJOR STOCK MARKET MOVEMENTS OVERNIGHT - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: MAJOR STOCK MARKET MOVEMENTS OVERNIGHT - AUG 8.

text.p: NEW YORK - Wall Street stocks fell to session lows in late afternoon on Thursday, weighed by a weakening tone in the bond market.
The Dow industrials fell 56 points to 8203, triggering program trading curbs on the New York Stock Exchange at 1451 EDT/1851 GMT.
A slumping bond market pressured stocks. The 30-year U.S. Treasury fell 15/32 to yield 6.52 percent after briefly rallying at the conclusion of the Treasury's quarterly refunding auction.
"We're caught in a bout of profit-taking here," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "For the moment, stocks appear to be following bonds."

LONDON - Britain's leading blue- chip index charged further into record ground as investors cheered a signal from the Bank of England that its quarter-point interest rate hike was likely to be the last for a while, strategists and dealers said. The FTSE 100 closed at 5086.8, up 60.6 points, or 1.21 percent.

FRANKFURT - An overnight rally on Wall Street lifted the mood on the wary German share market, helping to push prices to healthy gains. The DAX-30 index closed at 4414.35, up 78.96 points, or 1.82 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4428.08, up 63.83 points, or 1.46 percent.
PARIS - French shares finished higher after tracking a rise on Wall Street to record levels. The CAC-40 index closed at 3056.34, up 19.25 points, or 0.63 percent.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed sharply higher, powered by firmer U.S. financial markets, a strong dollar and positive company results, dealers said. The Swiss market index closed at 5922.1, up 110.0 points, or 1.89 percent.

MILAN - Italian shares ended higher reflecting a firmer start to Wall Street and record levels on London stocks, but the FIB30 futures contract showed less impressive gains as some caution took hold. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 14822, up 131 points, or 0.89 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Dutch shares jumped to a new record close above 1,000 points, despite a fall of index heavyweight Royal Dutch which announced disappointing second quarter results, dealers said. The AEX index closed at 1010.97, up 18.08 points, or 1.82 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed lower, with the key market index finishing below the 19,500 mark for the first time since May 1. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19475.85, down 226.22 points, or 1.15 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index continued its record-breaking run, climbing 131.67 points, or 0.80 percent to a record close of 16,673.27. The Hang Seng index closed at 16673.27, up 131.67 points, or 0.80 percent.

SYDNEY - Bellwether Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd led the Australian share market to a lower close as traders expressed concern about the costs and direction of its mineral division. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2717.7, down 9.4 points, or 0.34 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Strong foreign buying and futures-driven trade hoisted South African shares to new highs, pushing the all-share index above the 7,600 level for the first time in big turnover trade. The All-share index closed at 7614.4, up 67.6 points, or 0.90 percent. The All Gold index closed at 967.1, up 10.1 points, or 1.06 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9314.2, up 67.1 points, or 0.73 percent.
